annotations.text: FOUR DIRECTIONS FOR MEGACHAT — the same browse/home screen four ways. They differ in organizing idea, not just colour: a feed of proof, a poster bill, a calm grid, a video wall. Notes sit under each frame. Sample numbers throughout — handles invented, amounts plausible placeholders. Pick one and I'll build it across the real screens.

A · LEDGER — the proof IS the aesthetic. One feed, hairline rules, no cards; live rooms and bounty pools are entries in the same ledger, and the verification strip never leaves the screen.
Why: the only one that looks like what we actually built — evidence, tiers, codes read off a broadcast.
Tradeoff: reads as a terminal; cold for a fan who just wants on the show.

B · MARQUEE — a bill, not a dashboard. Streamer names at poster scale in a serif; bounties are a side column of people who aren't here yet.
Why: the most personality, and it puts the human first — buying a seat feels like a gig listing.
Tradeoff: hides the machinery; trust has to be earned elsewhere.

C · SIGNAL — the safe modern one. Light, disciplined, one accent, live state as a 7px dot instead of a glow.
Why: most legible, least likely to age; a streamer landing on a share link trusts it instantly.
Tradeoff: you have seen it before — that is why it works and why it isn't memorable.

D · BOOTH — the product is the interface. 48px of chrome, everything else is video; rate and seats ride the tile as a broadcast lower-third; bounties run as a bottom rail.
Why: what you're buying is being on camera, so show the cameras.
Tradeoff: needs real feeds — the tiles are placeholders, and dead rooms look worst here.
